subject.title: Gateway silently skips channel initialization on plugin/runtime mismatch or missing module files

question: Should Gateway treat configured channel plugin load failures as startup-blocking errors, structured WARN-level health failures, or best-effort background diagnostics?
rationale: The report asks for fail-fast compatibility checks, audit summaries, hot reload, and warning-level health output; code can implement any of those, but the user-visible startup contract and upgrade behavior need maintainer intent first.

options.title: Structured warn-and-continue health summary
options.body: Record every configured channel attempt and emit a startup summary with failed channel ids and reasons while preserving current best-effort Gateway startup behavior.

options.title: Fail fast for configured channel failures
options.body: Make configured channel plugin load or compatibility failures abort startup with a clear error, accepting a stricter upgrade and operator impact.

options.title: Split into narrower follow-ups
options.body: Keep this umbrella issue as maintainer review context and move missing-module warnings, Feishu timeout health, hot reload, and performance caching into separate scoped issues.

recommendation.title: Structured warn-and-continue health summary
recommendation.body: Record every configured channel attempt and emit a startup summary with failed channel ids and reasons while preserving current best-effort Gateway startup behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current startup loop and plugin diagnostic path blame to this source-carrier history, making this the best available routing owner for the startup contract choice.
